name: NotebookLM
pros: Closed-source reasoning dramatically reduces hallucination beyond the source set
Citations back to exact passages support verification
Audio overviews are a genuinely novel output format
files: PDF, Google Docs, Google Slides, web URLs, YouTube links, and pasted text.
value: Upload documents, paste text, or link sources, and NotebookLM answers questions, summarizes, and generates content grounded only on what you gave it, not on general training data. The closed-source property is the point.
engine: Google's Gemini models, operating over user-provided sources.
latency: Fast for question answering. Audio overview generation takes a few minutes.

pricing.includes: Notebooks up to 50 sources, 25M tokens per notebook

pricing.model: Per-seat monthly (Google One AI Premium or Workspace)
pricing.includes: More notebooks, higher limits, team sharing

quality: Strong citation accuracy back to source passages. Stays within sources rather than hallucinating beyond them.
tagline: Research assistant that reasons over documents you provide, not the web.
use_cases: Analyzing a set of documents without the model reasoning outside them
Research synthesis across multiple sources with citations back to the exact passage
Generating audio overviews (podcast format) from uploaded source material
integrations: Web and YouTube as source types
governance_note: The closed-source behavior is the main governance argument for it: the model's answers are grounded on what you uploaded and cite back to passages, which makes hallucination outside the source set much less likely. The remaining question is the data path: documents uploaded to the consumer product are under Google's consumer terms; the same documents in a Workspace deployment are under enterprise terms. Confidential material should only go into a Workspace-governed instance.
training_optout: Google's data terms apply. Consumer tier data handling differs from Workspace. Confirm before uploading confidential material.
